symptom: The standalone deny-only Ed25519 mathematics probe built the untrusted proof request before snapshotting the caller-owned signature claim. A descriptor-triggered mutation during envelope preflight could replace an initially wrong public key or signature with the matching value before the late claim snapshot, reporting signatureMathConsistent=true for a different entry-time claim. No independent authority or scoring was granted.
lesson: Even a mathematical-consistency flag can be laundered when caller-owned signature data is first captured after an unrelated request builder invokes descriptor traps. A later valid key or signature is not the caller claim present before preflight.
guardrail: Snapshot the complete strict own-data-descriptor Ed25519 claim before building the request; use that pinned claim for all signature fields and retain existing request-not-ready precedence. Add phase-triggered negative tests for both key and signature swaps, assert the mutation really executed, and keep independentAuthorityVerified=false and scoringAuthorized=false on every path.
